reason: The capillary sleeves explicitly show an empty inner face for the endothelial layer, so this is a clear place to start building the route.
expectation: The lining and sleeves should form a capillary network.

effect: The lining and sleeves made a capillary bed; its thin walls allow exchange with surrounding fluid. I can now build the larger vessels.
reaction: The connection between thin walls and exchange makes sense.
reason: The arterial wall needs an inner lining, so combining it with the endothelial lining is a reasonable next step.
expectation: This should make an artery with a lined interior and thick outer wall.

effect: The lining and arterial wall formed arteries with elastic walls that stretch and recoil. The remaining vessel wall still needs a lining.
reaction: The pulse-and-rest picture helps explain why the wall is elastic.
reason: The venous wall should also need an endothelial lining to form a vessel.
expectation: This should make lined venous vessels, which can then receive the valve folds.

effect: The endothelial lining and venous wall formed thin-walled veins. The valve folds can now be added.
reaction: The vein's wide, thin wall contrasts clearly with the artery's thick elastic wall.
reason: The picture shows the valve folds inside a vein, so they belong with the newly made veins.
expectation: The folds should fit inside the veins to form valves.

effect: The valves formed a venous return route; the picture shows muscle compression helping move blood toward the heart while valves resist backflow.
reaction: The muscle-and-valve partnership was a useful detail.
reason: The goal is to connect the vessels through tissues, so the arteries and capillary bed are a logical next pair.
expectation: The arteries should connect to the capillary bed, leaving the venous return to complete the route.

effect: The arteries now branch into a capillary bed beside tissue cells; the venous return remains to complete the route.
reaction: The branching picture makes the distribution route clear.
reason: Connecting the venous return should provide the path back from the capillary bed.
expectation: The vessels should form a route through the tissues and back toward the heart.

effect: The capillaries now connect arteries to veins, completing the route through tissues and back toward the heart.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate vessels form one continuous network.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the vein valves was most worthwhile: the picture showed how contracting muscles and valves help blood return toward the heart.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the lined veins felt fairly predictable after making the arteries, though it was needed for the network.

surprise.text: I was surprised that nearby limb muscles help move blood through veins as the valves resist backward flow.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goal gave the vessel parts clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the completed vessel network connects with the heart and other organs; putting the route together made me curious about the larger system.
